old: Built from a structural test article (STA-099) converted to flight after Enterprise was deemed too expensive to upgrade. First flew STS-6 (1983-04-04) carrying out the first Shuttle EVA. Flew 10 missions in total: STS-6, STS-7, STS-8, STS-41-B, STS-41-C, STS-41-G, STS-51-B, STS-51-F, STS-61-A, and final flight STS-51-L. On 1986-01-28, STS-51-L launched at unprecedented cold (−1 °C) — the right SRB's O-rings failed to seal, hot gas burned through the strut attaching the SRB to the external tank, and the orbiter broke apart at Max-Q (T+73s) at 14 km altitude. All seven crew perished including Sally Ride from her groundbreaking STS-7 mission. The Rogers Commission ground the Shuttle for 32 months and rewrote NASA's safety culture.
